title: The texts of MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-012 and the message ID of a refused rule-model read are not specified
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.3.1 (VR-P7-001-2, MSG-P7-003), A2.2.4.3 (AC-EXC-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-05 naming ruleVersion and decisionCode) and A2.1.4.3; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 AC-EXC-P3-037-01 (chainVerified false with warning MSG-P7-012); TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.2 (API-P7-006 and API-P7-007 errors 401, 403, 503); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}) and slide 27 (checksum verified by the owning service)
description: Three message values this slice needs are missing from every source read. The IDs MSG-P7-009 (a record refused for a missing rule version or an unknown decision code) and MSG-P7-012 (an entry that does not verify against the chain) are named by the FSD but no source gives their text, so the problem detail and the page warning cannot be written from the documents. The rule-model read has no message at all: the architecture and the Temporal and Drools design say a version that is not in force, or a model whose checksum does not match, is refused rather than served, but no source names the message ID or the status the refusal answers.
evidence: FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 rows AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 name MSG-P7-009 and the field, with no text; FSD P3 v4 AC-EXC-P3-037-01 names MSG-P7-012 as a warning, with no text; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 list no rule-model operation and so no message; no message catalogue is in the sources read; Architecture v5 slide 27 and Temporal and Drools slide 15 state the refusal without naming its message
owner_role: Solution architect with the P7 TechX squad
proposed: The P7 message catalogue fixes the text of MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-012 and allocates the ID of the rule-model refusal (a version not in force, or a checksum mismatch) with its status; this story then cites the three texts in place of the placeholder

title: The rule-model read is not in the P7 API inventory, and its path parameters and response body are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-decision IN: POST /rule-models and GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}) and slide 27 (Load: GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 notes (each owning service fetches the model with GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} and verifies the checksum); TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 appendix T-A.1 (eight endpoints, none of them a rule-model read)
description: The architecture gives rwb-decision a rule-model read for the owning services and both the narrative slides and the Temporal and Drools design call it on the hot path of every evaluation, but the P7 appendix T-A.1 inventory holds no such operation: the eight paths are the recommendation, the approvals and the decision-log pair. The path parameters are written {n}/{v} in the architecture and package code and version label in the design, no source gives the response body (the compiled DRL, the KieBase artifact or a reference to it), the content type, the caching header or the status and problem shape of a refused read. A consuming service cannot be coded against the operation from the documents alone.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (IN line: POST /rule-models, GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}) and slide 27 (RUN IN THE OWNING SERVICE: Load GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 notes; TSD P7 v2 appendix T-A.1 rows API-P7-001 to API-P7-008, none a rule-model read; the Ownership Map holds the /admin/rule-package* paths and no /rule-models entry
proposed: Publish the rule-model read in the rwb-decision OpenAPI 3.1 document and the P7 appendix: path /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}, the response body with packageCode, versionLabel, status, validFrom, checksum and the compiled model, and the 422 and 404 problems; the owning services then build against it and its fake

title: decision_log_entry is modelled with a foreign key to recovery_case, a uuid case_id and no business-date column
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-002 case_id, CROSS_REF uuid, required No) and T3.3 (decision_log_entry.case_id to recovery_case, many to 0 or 1); Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-DEC-002, DF-DEC-008 inputs_ref example inputs/2026-12-03/7f3a); legacy story RWB-E1-018 flow step 11 and BR8 (the entry carries the ALS business date); Template and Rules v1 DP-01 and R5.5
description: The monolith model makes the case a foreign key into recovery_case and types the column as a uuid, which cannot survive the split: rwb-decision holds its own schema, owns no case row and may not read one. No source says what the column becomes in the target, nor how the ALS business date the legacy record carries is held, because decision_log_entry has no business-date column and the legacy record needs one. A build that keeps the foreign key cannot deploy; a build that resolves the case on rwb-case would break the business-key rule of D-RCV-35 U4 and make the ledger depend on a live case.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-002 case_id, CROSS_REF, uuid, required No) and T3.3 (decision_log_entry -> case_id -> recovery_case, many to 0 or 1); the same TSD lists no business-date field on the table; legacy RWB-E1-018 flow step 11, BR8 and the decision-log column list of its section 11; D-RCV-35 U4 and ADR-010 hold the business-key rule; Template and Rules v1 DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables
owner_role: Solution architect with the P7 data owner
proposed: The rwb_decision baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP holds the case reference as an indexed business key with no foreign key, and the ALS business date is carried inside inputs_ref on the pattern of the FSD example inputs/2026-12-03/7f3a; if an audit query needs the date as a column, the store story adds it and this story cites it

title: The rule ID of the ENTER row of package ENTRY is not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-018 flow step 7, section 11 (DF-REF-002 rule_id, DF-REF-003 rule_version) and BR8 (the ENTRY rule ID is carried to the decision log); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 (each row is one rule whose name is the rule ID written to the decision record); FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 (rule ID R-UNI-14 as an example only)
description: The legacy story requires the ENTER rule ID on every case-creation record and the design says the rule ID is the name of the fired row, but no source lists a row name for package ENTRY. The EXCLUSION rows are named in the sources (EXCL-004 for ACTIVE_PLAN and EXCL-006 for OPEN_DISPUTE), so the naming pattern is visible yet the ENTER value cannot be derived from it without inventing one. The entry must carry the value the record carried; the literal is left to the registry.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-018 flow step 7 (the ENTER rule ID and package version are carried to the decision log) and section 3 (packages ENTRY and EXCLUSION in force); Temporal and Drools slide 16 (the row name is the rule ID, the worked example uses ALLOC-014); legacy AC2 and AC6 name EXCL-004 and EXCL-006, and no source names an ENTRY row
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with the P7 rule owner
proposed: RWB-P7-E1073-APP publishes the Rows tab of package ENTRY with its rule IDs, and rule_row.drools_rule_name holds them; until then the story asserts that the entry carries the rule ID the published record carried and test data cites no literal
